subject: tired office worker
title: What If You Worked 60 Hours Every Week?

scenes.text: What if you worked 60 hours every week? You'd get more done, but not much more.
A Stanford study of factory workers found output keeps pace with hours only up to about 49 a week.
After that, each extra hour adds less. Seventy hours produced barely more than fifty-six.
Your body pays too. Working 55 hours or more is linked to a 35 percent higher risk of stroke.
And a 17 percent higher risk of dying from heart disease, compared with a 35 to 40 hour week.
The WHO linked long hours to about 745,000 deaths in one year. The extra hours cost more than they earn.

description:
What if you worked 60 hours every week? Economist John Pencavel (Stanford) found munitions workers' output rose with hours up to about 49 a week, then grew more slowly; 70 hours produced little more than 56.
A 2021 WHO/ILO study linked working 55 or more hours a week to a 35 percent higher risk of stroke and 17 percent higher risk of dying from heart disease, and to about 745,000 deaths in 2016.
